fields.value: Live view of runs: local server for one developer, shared server for a team

Design how Etude shows runs while they are still going, for a single developer and for a team, then deliver a first milestone that includes the table stake: a link to a run that is still running.

## Why

Weights & Biases users take a link to a live run for granted. Etude has `etude report --serve`, which is local, has no login and reads sealed files. The link is one feature of a bigger system: where Etude's state lives as it grows from one laptop to a team.

## Direction

Jack Heart, 2026-11-13:

"For live link the biggest issue is that, so far, I've intended the idea that you can scale up Etude from something that doesn't require a live server. You can just run it as a way of just launching machines from your local laptop to do some very basic training and check in on things. I'm okay to say that it involves running a server locally. I think that's not a problem.

I do want to avoid requiring hosting some sort of shared server and database. We do want to move to where we expect that, if you are working on a team, then that team would want to have a shared server and database and be able to see all the active runs and all that. I think it's time to start building towards that.

The live link would go to two different places and the UX around that would be different in those two cases. I'm sure we need to make sure that you get the ideal experience in both the single-developer and the hosted-team world"

And on scope: "these both deserve their own tasks, but they are bigger than just that. lets frame the task as design the bigger system, make progress towards it, make sure first milestone includes these tablestakes".

## Outcome

1. A design for the two worlds and the path between them:
   * Single developer: a local server is acceptable; no shared server or database is required. What the link is, what it shows, how fresh it is.
   * Team: a shared server and database that shows every active run. What moves there, what stays as files in the bucket, how a developer goes from the first world to the second without redoing anything.
   * What the link points at in each world and how the experience differs.
2. A first milestone, built: a link to a run that is still going, in the single-developer world, shaped so the team world is an addition and not a rewrite.

## Constraints

* "The files are the record" holds in both worlds: runs stay readable from the directory or bucket with no server.
* Tracking still works with no launcher and no server.
* The sibling Task on the machine model owns machines and their metrics; this Task owns where runs are viewed. Their designs must agree on what a run page shows.

## Context

Comparison and positioning notes: `scratch/explore.html` and `scratch/positioning.md` in the Manabot worktree `manabot.aa55a0-move-run-execution` (MTG-329). Existing pieces: `etude report --serve` (`src/etude/cli.py`), rows not yet sealed are not read (`docs/tracking.md`), the optional SSH controller (`src/etude/launch/controller.py`).
